trip.title: Low Desert Loop — January
trip.subtitle: Death Valley · Route 66 · Palm Springs · Anza-Borrego · Joshua Tree · Lake Havasu
trip.start_end: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)
trip.summary: A clockwise loop out of Las Vegas that never climbs out of the warm. Death Valley first, then down across the Mojave onto Route 66, over to the Coachella Valley and Anza-Borrego, up to Joshua Tree, and home along the Colorado River. Nothing on this route sleeps above 2,200 feet, so no night is expected to freeze. Two versions are priced: a motorhome build and a car-plus-hotels build.

itinerary.headline: Below sea level by lunchtime
itinerary.notes: Pick up the vehicle and drive straight in. Furnace Creek sits 190 feet below sea level and is the warmest place you will sleep all trip — January highs in the mid-60s, lows around 40.

itinerary.headline: The valley floor
itinerary.notes: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America. Artist's Drive is a one-way loop through mineral-stained hills and is limited to vehicles under 25 feet.

itinerary.headline: Dunes at sunrise
itinerary.notes: Mesquite Flat is twenty minutes up the valley and is best before the wind picks up. Dante's View is the one genuinely cold thing on this whole route — 5,450 feet, and it can be 25 degrees colder than where you parked this morning.

itinerary.headline: Out of the valley and onto Route 66
itinerary.notes: The one leg that looks dull on the map, and is not. You leave Death Valley by the southern road, cross the Mojave and land on the original alignment of Route 66. Calico is a silver town that went bust in 1896 and was rebuilt as a park — kitsch, and the kids will love it.

itinerary.headline: Into the warmest air on the trip
itinerary.notes: Start on the old road for Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch — a forest of welded steel trees hung with thousands of glass bottles, free, and unlike anything else on either route. Then over the pass and down into the Coachella Valley, which runs to the low 70s in January.

itinerary.headline: Palms, and snow you can go and look at
itinerary.notes: The tramway climbs from 2,600 feet to 8,500 in ten minutes. You can be in shirtsleeves at the bottom and in snow at the top on the same afternoon, which is the only snow anybody will see on this trip. Indian Canyons is Agua Caliente land — a real palm oasis in a desert canyon, on a walk that suits everyone.

itinerary.headline: Down the Salton Sea into Anza-Borrego
itinerary.notes: A short day along the west shore of the Salton Sea — a lake 230 feet below sea level that exists only because an irrigation canal broke in 1905 and took two years to close. Borrego Springs is a town of three thousand people surrounded on every side by the largest state park in California.

itinerary.headline: Six hundred thousand acres of state park
itinerary.notes: Borrego Palm Canyon is a three-mile round trip to a palm grove and, in a wet year, a waterfall. The Slot is a genuine slot canyon you walk yourself — no permit, no guide, no fee. Font's Point looks out over the Borrego Badlands and is the best view in the park, but the road to it is four miles of soft sand.

itinerary.headline: Up out of the low desert to Joshua Tree
itinerary.notes: You climb about 1,500 feet, and this is the first night that feels properly cool — high 30s rather than the high 40s you have had. Come in by the south entrance and the Cholla Cactus Garden is the first thing you meet.

itinerary.headline: A full day in Joshua Tree
itinerary.notes: Two deserts meet inside this park — the low Colorado and the high Mojave — and the Joshua trees only grow on the high side. Nearly everything worth doing is a short walk from a car park, which is exactly what you want on day ten with six people.

itinerary.headline: Amboy Crater and the empty Route 66
itinerary.notes: North on Amboy Road onto the loneliest surviving stretch of Route 66. Amboy Crater is a 250-foot cinder cone you can walk into. Roy's Motel is one neon sign in an empty town and it is the photograph everybody takes. Then east to the Colorado River.

itinerary.headline: A day on the water
itinerary.notes: Lake Havasu runs to the mid-60s in January — warm enough to be out on a boat, too cold to swim. London Bridge is the actual bridge that stood over the Thames from 1831: bought from the City of London in 1968, taken apart, and rebuilt here block by numbered block.
activities: Boat or kayak on the lake

itinerary.headline: Route 66 and the dam
itinerary.notes: Up to Kingman, where Route 66 crosses the highway, then down US-93 to Hoover Dam and into Las Vegas. In a car you can take the Oatman Highway instead — 23 miles longer, an hour slower, and the wild burros come to the window.

itinerary.headline: Return and depart
itinerary.notes: Allow half a day for the vehicle return process.

practical_notes.warm_weather: No night on this route is expected to freeze. The coldest stops are Barstow and Twentynine Palms, both around 2,000 feet, where January lows average the high 30s. A cold snap can put either a degree or two below freezing for a few hours before dawn, so pack for 35°F nights — but there is no sustained freeze anywhere, and nothing here needs winterising.
practical_notes.booking_order: Book Palm Springs first, then Borrego Springs, then Lake Havasu. January is high season in the Coachella Valley — the exact opposite of the Southwest Loop, where the cold made everything cheap. Death Valley and Twentynine Palms have far more slack.
practical_notes.fuel: California fuel runs well above Nevada and Arizona. Fill up in Nevada before you drive in, top off in Barstow rather than inside Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive, and fill again in Arizona on the way home.
practical_notes.death_valley_closures: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.
practical_notes.fonts_point: The road to Font's Point is four miles of soft sand off the Borrego Salton Seaway. It needs four-wheel drive and it strands two-wheel-drive vehicles regularly. A minivan will not make it. Either rent something suitable for the day, take a local jeep tour, or accept that this one is off the list.
practical_notes.oatman_highway: The Oatman Highway over Sitgreaves Pass is steep with blind hairpins, and most rental agreements effectively prohibit it. It is passable but tight in a car and out of the question in a motorhome. The I-40 route to Kingman is the one in the plan.
practical_notes.mileage_fees: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,365 miles adds roughly $480. Always price the unlimited-miles package as an alternative.
practical_notes.state_parks: The America the Beautiful pass covers Death Valley and Joshua Tree. It does not cover Anza-Borrego or the Salton Sea, which are California state parks, or Lake Havasu, which is an Arizona state park. None of them are expensive; they are just not free.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Death Valley — Artist's Drive and the final climb to Dante's View
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: A 30-footer is blocked. A C25 measures 24.93 ft — a three-inch margin, so measure the actual unit at pickup.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Route 66 — Oatman Highway over Sitgreaves Pass
vehicle_restrictions.rule: Steep with blind hairpins. Most rental agreements effectively prohibit it.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: Avoid. Take I-40 to Kingman instead, which is the routing in the plan.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_car: Passable but tight, and worth doing for the burros. Check your rental agreement first.

vehicle_restrictions.rule: Most sites inside the park cap at around 25 to 35 feet and there are no hookups, no dump station and, at most campgrounds, no water.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: Stay in Twentynine Palms instead, where a full-hookup site costs about the same and you can shower. The park's roads themselves are fine.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Anza-Borrego — the road to Font's Point
vehicle_restrictions.rule: Four miles of soft sand off the Borrego Salton Seaway. Four-wheel drive only.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_car: Blocked in a minivan or a two-wheel-drive SUV. This one is off the list for both builds unless you rent something else for the day.

money_savers.detail: Day use is $10 at the visitor centre and campground, and The Slot, Font's Point and every roadside trailhead are free. The Southwest Loop's equivalent — a guided slot canyon at Antelope — runs about $580 for six.
A hundred and thirty life-size metal sculptures — sloths, raptors, horses and a 350-foot serpent — scattered across open land around Borrego Springs. No gate, no ticket, no opening hours.

money_savers.item: Twentynine Palms instead of inside Joshua Tree
money_savers.detail: The park's own campgrounds have no hookups, no dump and mostly no water. A full-hookup site in town costs about the same as a dry site inside and you can shower — and you are ten minutes from the north entrance either way.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.

money_savers.item: Go midweek in the Coachella Valley
money_savers.detail: January is peak season in Palm Springs and the weekend premium is steep. Arriving Sunday or Monday rather than Friday is the single biggest lever in the lodging line.

Covers Death Valley and Joshua Tree — both national parks on this route. It does NOT cover Anza-Borrego or the Salton Sea, which are California state parks, or Lake Havasu, which is an Arizona state park.

rejected_alternatives.place: Zion, Bryce and the Grand Canyon
rejected_alternatives.reason: The famous parks on the Southwest Loop sit between 4,000 and 8,000 feet. Warm and high do not go together in January — that is the entire reason this route exists.
5,200 feet, freezing at night in January, and on the wrong side of the map. It belongs to the Southwest Loop.
Warmer still, and the giant saguaro grows nowhere on this route. But reaching Tucson from Las Vegas costs you a 288-mile day. That trip is the Sonoran Loop.
No hookups, no potable water, no cell service, and the York Fire burned close to 100,000 acres in 2023 including much of the Cima Dome Joshua tree forest.
Genuinely remarkable, and only twenty minutes past the south end of the Salton Sea — but it sits on the far shore and adds about 70 miles to the shortest day of the trip.
A 110-mile round trip from Furnace Creek for a single crater. It fits when Death Valley gets four nights, not three.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheapest, simplest, and no longer the cold one

vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. On this route there is no reason to take the smaller C25 for clearance — the only length limit you meet is Death Valley's 25 ft on Artist's Drive and Dante's View, and a C25 measures 24.93 ft, which is a three-inch margin you should not rely on.

lines.basis: Includes protection, unlimited miles and 15 generator hours. Kit fee declined.
1,365 mi at 8 mpg. California fuel runs well above Nevada and Arizona, so $4.40-4.90/gal blended
13 nights, full hookups. California parks run higher than the Southwest Loop's Utah and Arizona sites
Cooking in the RV with a few meals out
Bought in Vegas on day 1 instead of paying per-person kit fees
Days 1-4 economy car; the 30-footer is barred from Artist's Drive and Dante's View
Six tickets. The one paid attraction that everybody agreed was worth it
Anza-Borrego, the Salton Sea and Lake Havasu are state parks — the national park pass is not valid at any of them
America the Beautiful annual pass already owned — covers Death Valley and Joshua Tree

pros: Food costs stay low because you cook
No freezing nights, so none of the winterising grief the Southwest Loop forces on you
Only two places on this route it cannot go, and both are in Death Valley
cons: Still barred from Artist's Drive and Dante's View, so it still needs a separate rental car for days 1-4
Cannot take the Oatman Highway on the way home
Joshua Tree's own campgrounds are too small and have no hookups, so you sleep in town
Tanks fill fast with six people; plan a dump roughly every other night
Palm Springs and Borrego Springs RV parks are at their annual peak in January

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: More expensive, more comfortable, and it unlocks the Oatman Highway

vehicle.notes: A minivan is better for people, a Suburban better for luggage. Fourteen days from Las Vegas including airport concession fees. Neither will get you to Font's Point — that needs four-wheel drive.

fuel.basis: 1,365 mi at 18-20 mpg — a large saving over the RV even at California prices

lodging.basis: 13 nights, two rooms or one rental house. January is high season in Palm Springs and Borrego Springs, which is what makes this line bigger than the Southwest Loop's

food.basis: Eating out for six. This single line is most of the gap between the two options.

pros: Unlocks the Oatman Highway and its burros on the way home
Real beds, and rooms you can spread six people across
No dump station, no propane, no levelling blocks
Artist's Drive and Dante's View without a second rental
cons: Roughly $2,000 to $5,300 more than the motorhome
Six separate lodging bookings to manage, in the region's most expensive month
Luggage for six in one vehicle for two weeks is tight
